question: Can a decoder-only transformer internalize latent rules over memorized facts without verbalizing intermediate steps, what changes during delayed generalization, and when does that mechanism transfer systematically to unseen facts?

key_findings.claim: Two-hop composition generalizes within the training fact distribution only after extreme delayed training, while held-out atomic facts remain unusable in new compositions.
key_findings.evidence: With 2,000 entities and inferred/atomic ratio 7.2, training accuracy exceeds 99% around 14K steps when ID test accuracy is at most 9.2%; ID accuracy approaches perfection only after about 50 times more optimization, whereas OOD composition remains at zero through two million steps.

key_findings.claim: The inferred-to-atomic example ratio, rather than absolute entity count, controls the relative delay in this construction, but this does not by itself refute all critical-data-size accounts of grokking.
key_findings.evidence: At fixed entity count, increasing phi makes ID generalization arrive earlier; at fixed phi, changing entity count leaves the gap in epochs qualitatively similar. These experiments co-vary token frequency, number of repeated rule applications, total optimization steps per epoch, and circuit storage demand, so the result supports a distributional driver in this setup rather than a universal replacement for data-size explanations.

anchors.section: Effect of ratio and data size

key_findings.claim: The proposed composition circuit retrieves a bridge entity in lower layers and performs the second lookup in upper layers; its duplicated fact storage explains the synthetic OOD failure and motivates cross-layer sharing.
key_findings.evidence: Logit-lens ranks and activation replacement identify bridge b at S[5,r1], delayed relation r2 at S[5,r2], and tail t at the final position. During grokking, the bridge-to-output causal effect and r2 decodability increase. Facts used only as OOD atoms are not learned in the upper-layer second-hop store. Sharing parameters between the first and last four layers eventually produces nonzero OOD composition accuracy.

key_findings.claim: Systematic generalization is task-dependent: comparison groks an OOD-capable parallel retrieval circuit because both operands use the same lower-layer fact store.
key_findings.evidence: On random entity-attribute-value facts, two values become decodable at S[5,e1] and S[5,e2], an attribute-specific label set is prepared at S[7,a], and upper layers select the comparison label. Because ID and OOD atomic facts are retrieved through the same parallel path, both ID and OOD test accuracy rise after grokking.

key_findings.claim: The parametric-versus-context-memory demonstration shows successful task-specific compilation, not that parametric memory is generally superior to retrieval or explicit reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: A transformer trained up to 96 hours on 563K task facts reaches 99.3%, while GPT-4-Turbo/Gemini receive 5.4K retrieved or 28.2K contextual facts at inference and score near chance. The systems differ in task-specific training, architecture, compute placement, supervision, and search procedure; only one synthetic attribute task and 150 evaluation queries are reported. CoT often fails, but no trained retriever, symbolic graph algorithm, fine-tuned LLM, or compute-matched baseline is evaluated.

method.core_idea: Train controlled GPT-2-style models on atomic facts mixed with a sampled set of rule-derived facts, evaluate held-out deductions over seen versus unseen atoms, and follow internal retrieval paths before and after grokking.
method.mechanism: Construct random two-hop knowledge graphs and ordinal comparison tables; vary the inferred/atomic ratio and entity count; train an 8-layer, 768-dimensional decoder with AdamW far beyond interpolation; use normalized logit lens and same-type token-replacement activation interventions to infer causal paths; test parameter sharing; and contrast compiled parametric memory with long-context/RAG prompting on a harder graph-search variant.
assumptions: Synthetic unique-token facts capture important aspects of parametric factual reasoning.
ID held-out deductions measure rule induction, while deductions over separately held-out atoms measure systematicity.
Top-1 token changes under activation replacement are a suitable causal-strength measure.
The identified sparse paths are faithful summaries despite possible distributed or redundant computation.
Number of stored facts is a useful proxy for circuit complexity and optimizer preference.
Extended AdamW training exposes capabilities relevant to realistic language-model pretraining.

techniques.role: Controls pressure to reuse latent rules rather than memorize derived tuples.
Separates rule interpolation from systematic application to unseen atoms.
Tests whether bridge entities, values, relations, and label sets are decodable at selected residual states.
Measures whether swapping a state activation changes the final top-1 answer.
Tests the proposed diagnosis that duplicated layer-specific memories block composition transfer.

evaluations.metric: training, ID held-out, and OOD held-atom accuracy over optimization
evaluations.result: near-perfect ID performance after long grokking; OOD remains zero for the vanilla model
evaluations.baseline: memorization point, phi/data/model-scale sweeps, and shared-parameter transformer

evaluations.metric: logit-lens MRR/recall and activation-swap top-1 alteration rate
evaluations.result: bridge/value decodability and selected causal links strengthen during grokking
evaluations.baseline: start versus end of grokking and other grid states

evaluations.result: grokked transformer 99.3%; prompted GPT-4-Turbo and Gemini variants 11.3-37.3%
evaluations.baseline: direct versus CoT, full context versus two-hop-neighborhood retrieval

limitations: Only two handcrafted rule families, short token sequences, and randomly generated closed-world knowledge are studied.
Entity-level OOD holds out only 5% or 10% of atomic tuples while their tokens and fact-completion examples still appear in training.
Most mechanistic averages use 300 training examples from one 8-layer configuration and do not include head/MLP-level circuit completeness checks.
Activation replacement is evaluated via top-1 changes, which loses graded logit effects and can miss redundant paths.
The fact-count efficiency argument is qualitative; parameter norm, description length, and direct circuit ablations are not used to prove circuit competition.
Training for up to 96 GPU hours makes the practical value of delayed generalization uncertain.
The long-context/RAG comparison is not task-training- or compute-matched.
Claims about current frontier LLMs are tied to 2024 model versions and prompting choices.
failure_modes: A memorizing model can score well on ID-derived tuples when relation/entity coverage makes test facts close to training combinations.
Duplicated layer-local fact stores fail whenever a fact is needed in a role it never occupied during training.
Shared parameters improve access but can introduce optimization interference and still learn OOD composition extremely slowly.
Logit-lens visibility can reflect a decodable correlate rather than the representation actually consumed downstream.
Replacing a token-aligned residual state may create an off-manifold hybrid even when the replacement token type is matched.
Grokking schedules may be too compute-intensive or unstable to survive larger vocabularies, noisier facts, and nonstationary knowledge.
A simple symbolic graph traversal would solve the hard comparison construction without either extensive pretraining or LLM search.
reusable_insights: Measure generalization separately over unseen combinations of known atoms and over genuinely role-shifted or held-out atoms.
Data mixtures can change the relative description length of memorizing and rule-reusing solutions even at fixed sample count.
Mechanistic diagnoses should yield architectural interventions; cross-layer sharing is a concrete example.
Parallelizing operand retrieval can improve systematicity by avoiding role-specific copies of the same knowledge.
Evaluate whether a learned circuit assimilates new facts after training, not only whether it solves a frozen synthetic world.
When comparing parametric and external memory, match task-specific training, retrieval quality, and total compute.
open_questions: Can an already-grokked circuit rapidly incorporate edited or newly introduced facts without full retraining?
Which inferred/atomic distributions minimize total compute rather than optimization steps or epochs to generalization?
Do head- and MLP-level causal scrubbing results confirm the proposed bridge and comparison circuits?
Can recurrence, shared K/V memory, or modular retrieval enable systematic composition at realistic scale?
Does the circuit-efficiency account predict grokking boundaries under noisy, contradictory, many-to-many, or multi-token facts?
How does implicit compilation compare with a trained graph retriever or neuro-symbolic executor under equal resources?

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking of Hierarchical Structure in Vanilla Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Murty et al. show delayed structural generalization and nonmonotonic depth effects on linguistic hierarchies; this paper moves to stored factual rules, distinguishes ID from held-atom OOD, and proposes explicit retrieval circuits.

competitive_landscape.title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
competitive_landscape.difference: Dziri et al. find linearized subgraph matching and complexity-dependent failure on arithmetic, logic grids, and dynamic programming; this paper demonstrates late-emerging reusable circuits on two compact fact-rule systems but confirms composition is not systematically transferred.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Large Language Models Latently Perform Multi-Hop Reasoning?
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. causally test bridge recall and second-hop use in pretrained LLMs and find strong first-hop but moderate, relation-dependent full traversal; this paper trains from scratch and observes a clear bridge circuit only after controlled grokking.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking in the Wild: Data Augmentation for Real-World Multi-Hop Reasoning with Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-publication application of the ratio hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: Abramov et al. raise the inferred/atomic ratio with synthetic—even factually incorrect—knowledge-graph edges and report 95-100% on 2WikiMultiHopQA; this paper establishes the ratio/circuit phenomenon on random graphs but does not test real factual data.

competitive_landscape.title: Is Grokking Worthwhile? Functional Analysis and Transferability of Generalization Circuits in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: He et al. report that grokked and non-grokked models can share the same reasoning path and that mature circuits poorly assimilate new knowledge, reframing grokking as fact integration rather than sudden circuit birth; this directly narrows the original formation-and-efficiency interpretation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Transformers acquire implicit reasoning through grokking; circuit configuration explains both delayed generalization and task-dependent systematicity, while parameter sharing can repair composition.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Controlled ratio/size sweeps, checkpointed logit-lens and activation interventions, comparison-versus-composition circuits, a parameter-sharing intervention, and the hard search task support the narrative.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The ID/OOD role split and cross-layer-memory diagnosis are valuable and unusually actionable. The proposed circuit-efficiency cause is suggestive rather than established, the parametric-memory comparison is confounded, and later transfer experiments weaken any interpretation that grokking creates a generally reusable reasoning algorithm.

reviewer_notes: Read all 22 pages, including scale/tokenization controls, complete circuit grids, weight-decay and sharing ablations, and hard-task construction. Primary arXiv, ACL, NeurIPS, ICML/OpenReview records were checked through 2026-08-23.
